decisions.choice: saying: what follows are the LORD's own words to Moses
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech (see 1:1). The speech that follows runs to verse 9 and gives the rules for the lamp and the bread kept in the tent of meeting.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("parla", "blasphéma", "lapidèrent"); passé composé at Readable ("a dit", "a insulté", "ont jeté")
decisions.reason: French narrative tense by level, as in the rest of the book. It applies to the speech openings (verses 1 and 13) and to the account of the blasphemer (verses 10-12 and 23); the laws use the future at Literal and Balanced and "doit" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Narration in the plain written style with the honorific for God ("말씀하셨다"); God speaks to Moses in 해라체 ("-하라", "-해야 한다"), and the laws he gives use 해라체 with "너" / "너희"
decisions.reason: As the Exodus-Deuteronomy term sheet sets for the laws, and as Leviticus 1 already does; recorded once for this batch (Leviticus 24-27). Where a law speaks of the offender or the buyer in the third person it takes the plain written style ("-해야 한다").

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán": "phán" for God speaking; God's commands to Israel with "các ngươi" and "phải" / "không được"; Moses addressed as "ngươi" (L) and "con" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choices for Leviticus 24-27, as the Pentateuch term sheet and Genesis set them: the divine name in capitals with "Gia-vê" as the setting alternative, "phán" kept for God, and the laws in the form a lawgiver uses to a people ("các ngươi ... phải"); Readable gives the same commands in shorter plain sentences.

decisions.choice: pure oil of olives, crushed: the finest, clearest olive oil
decisions.reason: "Crushed" (or "beaten") describes oil made by pounding olives rather than squeezing them in a press. The oil that runs off first is the clearest, and "pure" means free of dregs, so that it burns brightly with little smoke. The same oil is asked for in Exodus 27:20, and "crushed oil" goes with the daily offering in Exodus 29:40. The oil comes from the people: the lamp is kept burning with what all Israel gives.

decisions.choice: to make a lamp go up: to light the lamp so that its flame rises
decisions.reason: The verb is "make go up", used of lighting lamps because the flame rises from the wick (Exodus 25:37; 27:20; Numbers 8:2-3). It is the same verb used of making a burnt offering go up in smoke (1:9).

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, every night without a break
decisions.reason: Verse 3 says the lamp burns "from evening until morning", so "continually" means that it is lit every night without fail, not that it never goes out by day. The same word is used of the regular daily burnt offering, offered morning and evening (Exodus 29:42; Numbers 28:3-6), and of the incense burned when the lamps are tended (Exodus 30:7-8). In 1 Samuel 3:3 the lamp is still burning before dawn. These verses repeat Exodus 27:20-21 almost word for word.

decisions.choice: without fail
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "without fail" for "continually", so that the reader does not picture a lamp that never goes out (see m3). Literal keeps "continually".

decisions.choice: every night
decisions.reason: Readable adds "every night", taken from verse 3 ("from evening until morning"). It splits the verse into three short sentences.

decisions.choice: sans faute
decisions.reason: "Sans faute" (without fail) renders "continually" at Balanced and Readable, as the English does; "sans interruption" would suggest a lamp that never goes out by day (see m3).

decisions.choice: kupandisha taa
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of making the lamp "go up" (see m2) with "kupandisha"; Balanced and Readable say the lamp burns ("iwake", "kuwaka").

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (Literal), "이스라엘 백성" (Balanced), "이스라엘 사람들" (Readable) for the sons of Israel, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The term sheet sets these three forms; Korean "자손", "백성" and "사람들" already include women and men, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Korean, as in Leviticus 1.

decisions.choice: "등불을 늘 올라가게 하여라" for "to make a lamp go up continually"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the flame going up; Balanced and Readable say that the lamp is to burn without fail.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L); "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: Vietnamese "con cháu" and "dân" already include men and women, so the English gender setting has no Vietnamese counterpart here and through these chapters.

records.literal_gloss: From outside of the curtain of the testimony, in [the] tent of meeting, will arrange it Aaron from evening until morning before Yahweh continually; [a] statute forever for your generations.

en.L: Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening until morning before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually; [it is] a statute forever for your generations.
en.B: Aaron is to set it in order in the tent of meeting, outside the curtain in front of the testimony, so that it burns before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from evening until morning without fail. This is a permanent rule for all your generations.
en.R: Aaron must take care of the lamp in the meeting tent. It stands outside the curtain in front of the covenant box. He must keep it burning in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every night, from evening until morning. This is a rule for all time to come.

es.L: Fuera del velo del Testimonio, en la Tienda del Encuentro, la dispondrá Aarón desde la tarde hasta la mañana delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} continuamente; [es] estatuto perpetuo por {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} generaciones.

es.R: Aarón tiene que cuidar la lámpara en la Tienda del Encuentro. Está fuera de la cortina, delante del arca del pacto. Tiene que mantenerla encendida delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} cada noche, desde la tarde hasta la mañana. Esta es una norma para siempre.

fr.L: Hors du voile du Témoignage, dans la tente de la Rencontre, Aaron la disposera du soir au matin devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} continuellement ; [c’est] une loi perpétuelle pour vos générations.

fr.R: Aaron doit prendre soin de la lampe dans la tente de la Rencontre. Elle se trouve hors du rideau, devant l’arche de l’alliance. Il doit la faire brûler devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} chaque nuit, du soir au matin. C’est une règle pour toujours.

vi.L: Ở bên ngoài bức màn của chứng ước, trong Lều Hội Kiến, A-rôn phải sắp đặt nó từ chiều tối đến sáng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} luôn luôn; [đó là] luật lệ đời đời qua các thế hệ của các ngươi.
vi.B: A-rôn phải sửa soạn đèn trong Lều Hội Kiến, bên ngoài bức màn che phía trước hòm chứng ước, để đèn cháy trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} từ chiều tối đến sáng, không bao giờ gián đoạn. Đây là luật lệ đời đời cho các ngươi qua mọi thế hệ.
vi.R: A-rôn phải lo cho ngọn đèn trong Lều Hội Kiến. Đèn ấy đặt bên ngoài bức màn, phía trước hòm giao ước. Mỗi đêm, từ chiều tối đến sáng, A-rôn phải giữ cho đèn cháy trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Đây là luật cho các ngươi đến muôn đời.

ko.L: 증거의 휘장 바깥, 회막 안에서 아론은 저녁부터 아침까지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 늘 그것을 정돈해야 한다. [이것은] 너희 대대로 영원한 규례이다.
ko.B: 아론은 회막 안, 증거궤 앞에 드리운 휘장 바깥에서 그 등불을 정돈하여, 그것이 저녁부터 아침까지 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 끊이지 않고 타게 해야 한다. 이것은 너희가 대대로 지켜야 할 영원한 규례이다.
ko.R: 아론은 회막 안에 있는 등불을 돌보아야 한다. 그 등불은 언약궤 앞에 드리운 휘장 바깥에 있다. 아론은 저녁부터 아침까지 밤마다 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에서 그 등불이 꺼지지 않게 해야 한다. 이것은 너희가 앞으로 영원히 지켜야 할 규례이다.

decisions.choice: the veil of the testimony: the curtain that hangs in front of the ark
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the pair of stone tablets with the covenant written on them, kept in the ark (Exodus 25:16, 21; 40:20), so the ark itself can be called "the ark of the testimony" (Exodus 25:22). The veil hung in front of it and closed off the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:33). The lampstand stood outside the veil, in the holy place, on the south side opposite the table (Exodus 26:35; 40:24-25). On the curtain see 4:6; on the testimony, 16:13.

decisions.choice: arrange it: set the lamp in order, trim it and fill it
decisions.reason: The verb means to set things in their proper order. It is used of laying out the wood and the pieces of the offering on the altar (1:7-8) and of laying out the bread in verse 8. For the lamp it covers filling it with oil and trimming the wick so that it burns through the night. "It" is the lamp of verse 2.

decisions.choice: a statute forever for your generations: a rule for all time
decisions.reason: The same phrase as 3:17 and 17:7. The care of the lamp is not for the wilderness only; it is to go on in every generation.

decisions.choice: the covenant box
decisions.reason: Readable says "the covenant box" for "the testimony", since it is the box holding the covenant tablets that the curtain screens (see m1). Literal and Balanced keep "the testimony".

decisions.choice: so that it burns ... from evening until morning
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the arranging is for: the lamp burns through the night. Readable adds "every night" for "continually", as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: el arca del pacto
decisions.reason: For the English Readable "covenant box", Spanish uses the settled "el arca" with "del pacto", which says what it holds without introducing a new word for the ark.

decisions.choice: l'arche de l'alliance
decisions.reason: For the English Readable "covenant box", French uses the settled word for the ark, "l'arche", with "de l'alliance" to say what it holds; a new word such as "coffre" would read as a different object.

decisions.choice: sanduku la agano
decisions.reason: "Sanduku" is already the settled word for the ark, so the English Readable "covenant box" is simply "sanduku la agano".

decisions.choice: "증거의 휘장" (Literal), "증거궤 앞에 드리운 휘장" (Balanced), "언약궤 앞에 드리운 휘장" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The term sheet uses "증거" for the testimony and "증거궤" for the ark that holds it; Readable follows the English Readable's "covenant box" with the more familiar "언약궤".

decisions.choice: "너희 대대로 영원한 규례" for "a statute forever for your generations"; Readable "앞으로 영원히 지켜야 할 규례"
decisions.reason: "영원한 규례" is the term sheet's phrase for a lasting statute, as in Leviticus 10:9.

decisions.choice: the pure lampstand: the lampstand of pure gold
decisions.reason: The lampstand was hammered out of pure gold (Exodus 25:31-39; 37:17-24), and Exodus 31:8 and 39:37 call it "the pure lampstand" as this verse does. "Pure" here is the metal, though it also fits the holiness of everything in the tent. It had seven lamps on one stand (Exodus 25:37); so verse 2 speaks of "a lamp" and this verse of "the lamps".

decisions.choice: he: Aaron, as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The subject is Aaron, named in verse 3, and after him the high priest of each generation (Exodus 27:21 speaks of Aaron and his sons).

decisions.choice: pure gold
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "pure gold" for "pure", because the reader would not otherwise know what makes a lampstand pure (see m1). Literal keeps "the pure lampstand".

decisions.choice: "등잔대" for the lampstand; "순수한" (Literal), "순금" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "등잔대" is the term sheet's word; "촛대" suggests candles, which the tabernacle did not have. Balanced and Readable name Aaron, as the meaning decision explains, because Korean leaves the subject unclear otherwise.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ סֹ֔לֶת וְאָפִיתָ֣ אֹתָ֔הּ שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה חַלּ֑וֹת שְׁנֵי֙ עֶשְׂרֹנִ֔ים יִהְיֶ֖ה הַֽחַלָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take fine flour and you will bake it [into] twelve loaves; two tenths will be the loaf the one.

en.L: And you shall take fine flour and bake it [into] twelve loaves; two tenths [of an ephah] shall be in each loaf.
en.B: You are to take fine flour and bake it into twelve loaves. Each loaf is to contain {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}}.
en.R: Bake twelve loaves of bread from fine flour. Each loaf must be made with {{units:about 4 quarts|two tenths of an ephah}} of flour.

es.L: Y tomarás flor de harina y cocerás con ella doce tortas; dos décimas [de efa] tendrá cada torta.
es.B: Tomarás flor de harina y cocerás con ella doce panes. Cada pan llevará {{units:unos 4 litros|dos décimas partes de un efa}}.
es.R: Con harina fina cuece doce panes. Para cada pan hay que usar {{units:unos 4 litros|dos décimas partes de un efa}} de harina.

fr.L: Et tu prendras de la fleur de farine, et tu en cuiras douze pains ; deux dixièmes [d’épha] seront dans chaque pain.
fr.B: Tu prendras de la fleur de farine et tu en feras cuire douze pains. Pour chaque pain, il faudra {{units:environ 4 litres|deux dixièmes d’épha}}.
fr.R: Fais cuire douze pains avec de la farine fine. Pour chaque pain, il faut {{units:environ 4 litres|deux dixièmes d’épha}} de farine.

sw.L: Nawe utachukua unga laini na kuoka mikate kumi na miwili kwa unga huo; sehemu mbili za kumi [za efa] zitakuwa katika kila mkate.
sw.B: Utachukua unga laini na kuoka mikate kumi na miwili. Kila mkate utaokwa kwa unga {{units:kama lita 4|sehemu mbili za kumi za efa}}.
sw.R: Oka mikate kumi na miwili kwa unga laini. Kila mkate lazima utengenezwe kwa {{units:kama lita 4|sehemu mbili za kumi za efa}} za unga.

vi.L: Ngươi phải lấy bột mịn và nướng [thành] mười hai ổ bánh; mỗi ổ bánh sẽ là hai phần mười [ê-pha].
vi.B: Con phải lấy bột mịn nướng thành mười hai ổ bánh. Mỗi ổ bánh làm bằng {{units:khoảng 4,4 lít|hai phần mười ê-pha}} bột.
vi.R: Hãy dùng bột mịn nướng mười hai ổ bánh. Mỗi ổ phải làm bằng {{units:khoảng 4,4 lít|hai phần mười ê-pha}} bột.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 고운 가루를 가져다가 그것으로 빵 열두 개를 구워라. 빵 한 개는 십분의 이 [에바]로 해야 한다.
ko.B: 너는 고운 가루를 가져다가 빵 열두 개를 구워라. 빵 한 개에 {{units:4.4리터쯤|십분의 이 에바}}가 들어가야 한다.
ko.R: 고운 가루로 빵 열두 개를 구워라. 빵 한 개를 만드는 데 가루 {{units:4.4리터쯤|십분의 이 에바}}를 써야 한다.

decisions.choice: loaves: round, flat loaves of bread
decisions.reason: The word is used for ring-shaped or round loaves, perhaps pierced, used in several offerings (2:4; 7:12; 8:26). Nothing is said here about yeast; the grain offering made for the altar must be unleavened (2:11), but this bread is eaten by the priests and only the frankincense is burned (verse 7).

decisions.choice: twelve: one loaf for each tribe of Israel
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the number, but twelve is the number of the tribes, and the bread is said to come "from the sons of Israel" (verse 8). The high priest's breastpiece likewise carries twelve stones for the twelve tribes (Exodus 28:21).

decisions.choice: two tenths: two tenths of an ephah of flour, about four quarts
decisions.reason: An ephah was a dry measure of about half a bushel; a tenth of an ephah was the usual amount for one grain offering (5:11; 14:21). Each of these loaves takes twice that amount, so they were large loaves. The figure in modern measures is approximate (see 5:11; 14:10). "You" is Moses, who is told to see that the bread is made; verse 8 says the priest sets it out.

decisions.choice: about 4 quarts / two tenths of an ephah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in modern units by default, with "two tenths of an ephah" as the alternative in the Measures setting. Literal keeps the Hebrew measure and brackets "of an ephah", which the Hebrew leaves understood.

decisions.choice: tortas (L); panes (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "tortas", the word used for these round loaves in the grain offerings (2:4); Balanced and Readable say "panes", since these are large loaves of bread, the bread of verse 7.

decisions.choice: pains
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word is "gâteaux" for the small cakes of the grain offering (2:4), but these are large loaves of bread set before the LORD, and the English says "loaves"; French says "pains" at every level.

decisions.choice: {{units:4.4리터쯤|십분의 이 에바}}: metric by default, the ephah as the alternative
decisions.reason: Korean readers measure in litres, so the default is metric, as in the other Korean Old Testament books; an ephah is taken as 22 litres (term sheet), so two tenths is about 4.4 litres. Literal keeps the unit, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "빵" for the loaves
decisions.reason: As the Korean style guide: "빵" is the ordinary word for baked bread; "떡" is a rice cake in modern Korean.

decisions.choice: {{units:khoảng 4,4 lít|hai phần mười ê-pha}}
decisions.reason: Metric by default, as in French and Swahili, with the original measure as the alternative: an ephah taken as 22 litres (the Pentateuch measures), so two tenths is about 4.4 litres, written with a decimal comma. The English shows US quarts.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֛ם שְׁתַּ֥יִם מַֽעֲרָכ֖וֹת שֵׁ֣שׁ הַֽמַּעֲרָ֑כֶת עַ֛ל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֥ן הַטָּהֹ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will set them [in] two rows, six [in] the row, on the table the pure before Yahweh.

en.L: And you shall set them [in] two rows, six [in] a row, on the pure table before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Set them out on the pure gold table before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in two rows with six loaves to a row.
en.R: Put them on the table made of pure gold in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Put them in two rows, with six loaves in each row.

es.L: Y las pondrás [en] dos hileras, seis [en] cada hilera, sobre la mesa pura delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Los colocarás sobre la mesa de oro puro delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, en dos hileras de seis panes cada una.
es.R: Ponlos sobre la mesa de oro puro delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Ponlos en dos hileras, con seis panes en cada hilera.

fr.L: Et tu les placeras [en] deux rangées, six [par] rangée, sur la table pure devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Tu les disposeras sur la table d’or pur devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en deux rangées de six pains.
fr.R: Mets-les sur la table en or pur, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mets-les en deux rangées, avec six pains dans chaque rangée.

sw.L: Nawe utaiweka [katika] safu mbili, sita [katika] safu, juu ya meza safi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Utaipanga juu ya meza ya dhahabu safi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika safu mbili, mikate sita kila safu.
sw.R: Iweke juu ya meza ya dhahabu safi mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ipange katika safu mbili, mikate sita katika kila safu.

vi.L: Ngươi phải đặt chúng [thành] hai hàng, sáu [ổ] một hàng, trên cái bàn tinh khiết trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Con hãy bày bánh trên cái bàn bằng vàng ròng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thành hai hàng, mỗi hàng sáu ổ.
vi.R: Hãy đặt bánh trên cái bàn bằng vàng ròng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Xếp bánh thành hai hàng, mỗi hàng sáu ổ.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 그것들을 두 줄로, 한 줄에 여섯 개씩, {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞 순수한 상 위에 놓아라.
ko.B: 그것들을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞 순금 상 위에 한 줄에 여섯 개씩 두 줄로 차려 놓아라.
ko.R: 그 빵들을 순금으로 만든 상 위에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 놓아라. 두 줄로 놓되, 한 줄에 여섯 개씩 놓아라.

decisions.choice: rows: two arrangements of six loaves, either laid in rows or stacked in piles
decisions.reason: The word means an arrangement, from the verb "arrange" used in verses 3, 4 and 8. It can be a row or a pile. The table was small, about three feet long and a foot and a half wide (Exodus 25:23), so twelve large loaves may have been stacked in two piles. Frankincense was put "on the row" (verse 7). The text does not settle which arrangement is meant.

decisions.choice: the pure table: the table covered with pure gold
decisions.reason: The table was made of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold (Exodus 25:23-30; 37:10-16) and is called "the pure table" again in 2 Chronicles 13:11. Exodus 25:30 names its purpose: "you shall set the bread of the presence on the table before me always". The bread is "before the LORD" because it lay in the holy place, facing the lampstand, just outside the veil.

decisions.choice: pure gold
decisions.reason: As with the lampstand in verse 4, Balanced and Readable say "pure gold" so that the reader knows what "pure" refers to. Balanced and Readable keep "rows", with the footnote on m1.

decisions.choice: "줄" for the rows
decisions.reason: The meaning decision's footnote says the loaves may have been stacked in piles; Korean follows the English text with "줄" and leaves the other reading to the footnote.

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֥ עַל־הַֽמַּעֲרֶ֖כֶת לְבֹנָ֣ה זַכָּ֑ה וְהָיְתָ֤ה לַלֶּ֨חֶם֙ לְאַזְכָּרָ֔ה אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put on the row frankincense pure, and it will be for the bread as [a] memorial portion, [an] offering by fire to Yahweh.

en.L: And you shall put pure frankincense on [each] row, and it shall be for the bread as a memorial portion, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Put pure frankincense on each row. It is to be a memorial portion for the bread, a food offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Put pure frankincense on each row. The frankincense will be the part of the bread that is a reminder. It is a food offering burned on the fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y pondrás sobre [cada] hilera incienso puro, y será para el pan como porción memorial, ofrenda quemada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pondrás incienso puro sobre cada hilera. Será la porción memorial del pan, una ofrenda quemada {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Pon incienso puro sobre cada hilera. El incienso será la parte del pan que sirve de recuerdo. Es una ofrenda quemada en el fuego para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et tu mettras sur [chaque] rangée de l’encens pur, et il sera pour le pain une portion commémorative, une offrande consumée par le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Tu mettras de l’encens pur sur chaque rangée. Ce sera la portion commémorative du pain, une offrande consumée par le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Mets de l’encens pur sur chaque rangée. L’encens sera la part du pain qui sert de rappel. C’est une offrande brûlée sur le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nawe utaweka juu ya [kila] safu ubani safi, nao utakuwa kwa ajili ya mkate kuwa sehemu ya ukumbusho, sadaka ya kuteketezwa kwa moto kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Utaweka ubani safi juu ya kila safu. Utakuwa sehemu ya ukumbusho kwa ajili ya mkate, sadaka ya kuteketezwa kwa moto kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Weka ubani safi juu ya kila safu. Ubani huo utakuwa sehemu ya mkate ya kukumbusha. Ni sadaka iliyochomwa kwa moto kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ngươi phải đặt nhũ hương nguyên chất trên [mỗi] hàng, và nó sẽ dành cho bánh làm phần tưởng niệm, [là] của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Hãy đặt nhũ hương nguyên chất trên mỗi hàng bánh. Nhũ hương ấy là phần tưởng niệm thay cho bánh, là của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Hãy đặt nhũ hương nguyên chất trên mỗi hàng bánh. Nhũ hương ấy sẽ được đốt thay cho bánh, làm phần nhắc nhớ. Đó là của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: 그리고 너는 [각] 줄 위에 순수한 유향을 놓아라. 그것은 빵을 위한 기념 몫, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불로 바치는 제물이 될 것이다.
ko.B: 각 줄 위에 순수한 유향을 놓아라. 그것은 빵을 대신하는 기념 몫이 되어, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불로 바치는 제물이 될 것이다.
ko.R: 줄마다 순수한 유향을 놓아라. 그 유향은 빵 가운데서 기억하게 하는 몫이 된다. 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불에 태워 바치는 제물이다.

decisions.choice: a memorial portion for the bread: the frankincense is burned on the bread's behalf
decisions.reason: In the grain offering the memorial portion is the handful burned on the altar for the whole offering (2:2). Here the bread itself is eaten by the priests (verse 9), so it is the frankincense that is burned to the LORD in place of the bread. The text does not say when it was burned; the natural time is when the bread was changed each Sabbath (verse 8). Exodus 25:29 lists dishes and bowls that belonged to the table.

decisions.choice: pure frankincense: frankincense with nothing mixed in
decisions.reason: Frankincense is a fragrant resin (see 2:1). "Pure" is the same word used for the oil in verse 2: clean and unmixed. The incense of Exodus 30:34 also includes pure frankincense.

decisions.choice: pure frankincense: the Hebrew text has no other ingredient
decisions.reason: The Westminster Leningrad Codex reads only "pure frankincense". The Septuagint reads "pure frankincense and salt", perhaps from 2:13, which asks for salt with every grain offering. This translation follows the Hebrew text. Reviewers should check the Septuagint reading.

decisions.choice: each row
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "on the row", meaning each of the two rows. Literal brackets "each"; Balanced and Readable say "each row".

decisions.choice: the part of the bread that is a reminder
decisions.reason: Readable makes the frankincense the subject and calls it "the part of the bread that is a reminder", using the settled Readable wording for the memorial portion (see 2:2).

decisions.choice: "기념 몫" (Literal, Balanced), "기억하게 하는 몫" (Readable) for the memorial portion; "유향" for frankincense
decisions.reason: "몫" makes clear that the frankincense is the part burned for the bread; Readable unpacks "기념" with the plainer verb.

decisions.choice: "của lễ dâng bằng lửa" (food offering, offering by fire)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's rendering for this offering, used at every level through these chapters; it says how the offering reaches God, which the English Readable also spells out.

source.text: בְּי֨וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֜ת בְּי֣וֹם הַשַּׁבָּ֗ת יַֽעַרְכֶ֛נּוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד מֵאֵ֥ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] day of the sabbath, on [the] day of the sabbath he will arrange it before Yahweh continually, from the sons of Israel, [a] covenant forever.

en.L: On the sabbath day, on the sabbath day, he shall arrange it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} continually, from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, a covenant forever.
en.B: Every Sabbath day he is to set it out before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, without fail. It comes from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} as a covenant that lasts forever.
en.R: Every Sabbath day Aaron must set out fresh bread in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He must never fail to do it. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} give the bread as a sign of a covenant that will last forever.

es.L: En el día del sábado, en el día del sábado, lo dispondrá delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} continuamente, de parte de los hijos de Israel, pacto perpetuo.
es.B: Cada sábado colocará el pan en orden delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, sin falta. Viene de los israelitas como un pacto perpetuo.
es.R: Cada sábado Aarón tiene que poner pan fresco delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Nunca debe dejar de hacerlo. Los israelitas dan el pan como señal de un pacto que durará para siempre.

fr.L: Le jour du sabbat, le jour du sabbat, il le disposera devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} continuellement, de la part des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël : une alliance perpétuelle.
fr.B: Chaque jour de sabbat, il disposera le pain devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sans faute. Il vient des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, comme une alliance perpétuelle.
fr.R: Chaque jour de sabbat, Aaron doit mettre du pain frais devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Il ne doit jamais oublier de le faire. Les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} donnent ce pain comme signe d’une alliance qui durera toujours.

sw.L: Siku ya Sabato, siku ya Sabato, ataipanga mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} daima, kutoka kwa wana wa Israeli, agano la milele.
sw.B: Kila siku ya Sabato ataipanga mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} bila kukosa. Inatoka kwa Waisraeli kuwa agano la milele.
sw.R: Kila siku ya Sabato Haruni lazima aweke mikate mipya mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Asiache kufanya hivyo hata mara moja. Waisraeli wanatoa mikate hiyo kuwa ishara ya agano litakalodumu milele.

vi.L: Vào ngày Sa-bát, vào ngày Sa-bát, người phải sắp đặt nó trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} luôn luôn, [phần] từ con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên, [là] giao ước đời đời.
vi.B: Mỗi ngày Sa-bát, người phải bày bánh ấy trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, không bao giờ gián đoạn. Bánh ấy đến từ dân Y-sơ-ra-ên như một giao ước đời đời.
vi.R: Mỗi ngày Sa-bát, A-rôn phải bày bánh mới trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Người không bao giờ được bỏ qua việc này. Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên dâng bánh ấy làm dấu hiệu của một giao ước sẽ còn mãi mãi.

ko.L: 안식일마다, 안식일마다 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 늘 그것을 정돈해야 한다. [그것은] 이스라엘 자손에게서 [받는 것으로] 영원한 언약이다.
ko.B: 안식일마다 아론은 그것을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 끊이지 않고 차려 놓아야 한다. 이것은 이스라엘 백성이 바치는 것으로서 영원한 언약이다.
ko.R: 아론은 안식일마다 새 빵을 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 앞에 차려 놓아야 한다. 한 번도 거르면 안 된다. 이스라엘 사람들은 영원히 이어질 언약의 표로 이 빵을 바친다.

decisions.choice: on the sabbath day, on the sabbath day: every Sabbath
decisions.reason: Repeating the phrase means each Sabbath in turn. The bread stays on the table all week and is replaced every Sabbath; 1 Samuel 21:6 speaks of the old bread "removed from before the LORD, to put hot bread in its place". On the Sabbath see 23:3.

decisions.choice: from the sons of Israel: the bread is the people's gift and stands for them
alternatives: on behalf of the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: The flour and the oil are supplied by the people (verse 2), so the bread comes from them; the twelve loaves also stand for the twelve tribes before God (verse 5). The phrase can be read either way, and both are true of the bread.

decisions.choice: a covenant forever: a lasting sign of the covenant between God and Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the Sabbath itself (Exodus 31:16) and of circumcision (Genesis 17:13). The bread laid out before God each week is a standing reminder of the covenant: God's people are kept in his presence, and he provides for his priests from their gifts. The word for covenant can also mean the obligation the covenant lays on Israel.

decisions.choice: Aaron; fresh bread
decisions.reason: Readable names Aaron, the "he" of verses 3 and 4, and says "fresh bread", since each Sabbath new loaves replace the old (see m1).

decisions.choice: as a sign of a covenant
decisions.reason: Readable says the bread is given "as a sign of" the covenant, to explain how bread can be called a covenant (see m3).

decisions.choice: "안식일마다, 안식일마다" repeats the doubled Hebrew phrase
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repetition; "-마다" already gives its sense of "every Sabbath", which Balanced and Readable say once.

records.literal_gloss: And it will belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they will eat it in [a] place holy, for [a] most holy [thing] it [is] for him from [the] offerings by fire of Yahweh, [a] portion forever.

en.L: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it [is] a most holy [thing] for him from the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a portion forever."
en.B: The bread is to go to Aaron and his sons, and they must eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him, his permanent share of the food offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: The bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They must eat it in a holy place, because it is very holy. It is their share for all time from the food offerings burned on the fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

es.L: Y será para Aarón y para sus hijos, y lo comerán en un lugar santo, porque [es] cosa santísima para él de las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porción perpetua».
es.B: El pan será para Aarón y sus hijos, y lo comerán en un lugar santo, porque es santísimo para él: es su porción perpetua de las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}».
es.R: El pan es de Aarón y de sus hijos. Tienen que comerlo en un lugar santo, porque es muy santo. Es la parte que les toca para siempre de las ofrendas quemadas en el fuego para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}».

fr.L: Et il sera pour Aaron et pour ses fils, et ils le mangeront dans un lieu saint, car c’[est] une [chose] très sainte pour lui, [prise] sur les offrandes consumées par le feu {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : une part perpétuelle. »
fr.B: Ce pain reviendra à Aaron et à ses fils, et ils le mangeront dans un lieu saint, car c’est une chose très sainte pour lui, sa part perpétuelle des offrandes consumées par le feu {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Ce pain appartient à Aaron et à ses fils. Ils doivent le manger dans un lieu saint, car il est très saint. C’est leur part pour toujours des offrandes brûlées sur le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »

sw.L: Nayo itakuwa ya Haruni na ya wanawe, nao wataila mahali patakatifu, kwa kuwa [ni] kitu takatifu kabisa kwake kutoka katika sadaka za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} za kuteketezwa kwa moto, fungu la kudumu milele."
sw.B: Mikate hiyo itakuwa ya Haruni na wanawe, nao wataila mahali patakatifu, kwa sababu ni takatifu kabisa kwake, fungu lake la kudumu milele la sadaka za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} za kuteketezwa kwa moto."
sw.R: Mikate hiyo ni ya Haruni na wanawe. Lazima waile mahali patakatifu, kwa sababu ni takatifu sana. Ni fungu lao la milele la sadaka zilizochomwa kwa moto kwa ajili ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."

vi.L: Nó sẽ thuộc về A-rôn và các con trai người, và họ phải ăn nó tại một nơi thánh, vì nó [là một vật] chí thánh cho người, từ các của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, [là] phần đời đời."
vi.B: Bánh ấy thuộc về A-rôn và các con trai người, và họ phải ăn bánh tại một nơi thánh, vì đó là vật chí thánh dành cho người, là phần đời đời của người trong các của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.R: Bánh ấy thuộc về A-rôn và các con trai người. Họ phải ăn bánh ở một nơi thánh, vì bánh ấy rất thánh. Đó là phần của họ mãi mãi, lấy từ các của lễ dâng bằng lửa cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."

ko.L: 그리고 그것은 아론과 그의 아들들의 것이 될 것이니, 그들은 그것을 거룩한 곳에서 먹어야 한다. 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불로 바치는 제물 가운데서 그에게 지극히 거룩한 [것]이며, 영원한 몫이기 때문이다."
ko.B: 그 빵은 아론과 그의 아들들에게 돌아가며, 그들은 그것을 거룩한 곳에서 먹어야 한다. 그것은 지극히 거룩한 것이며, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불로 바치는 제물 가운데서 아론이 영원히 받을 몫이기 때문이다."
ko.R: 그 빵은 아론과 그의 아들들의 것이다. 그들은 그것을 거룩한 곳에서 먹어야 한다. 그것은 아주 거룩한 것이기 때문이다. 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 불에 태워 바치는 제물 가운데서 그들이 영원히 받을 몫이다."

decisions.choice: most holy: belonging wholly to God and handled only by the priests
decisions.reason: Things that are "most holy" may be eaten only by the priests, in a holy place (2:3; 6:10, 18; 10:12-13). The bread has lain before the LORD for a week, and like the grain offering it is now the priests' food. David and his men were given this bread when no other was at hand (1 Samuel 21:4-6), an event Jesus recalls (Mark 2:25-26).

decisions.choice: for him: for Aaron, as head of the priests
decisions.reason: "Him" is Aaron, who receives the bread for himself and his sons. The singular follows Aaron as the head of the priesthood, as in 6:10.

decisions.choice: a portion forever: the priests' permanent share
decisions.reason: The word means a set portion or allotment, as in 6:11 and 10:13-15. The bread counts among the food offerings, although only its frankincense is burned (verse 7).

decisions.choice: their share
decisions.reason: Readable says "their share", for Aaron and his sons together, where the Hebrew has "for him" (see m2).

decisions.choice: "지극히 거룩한 것" for "most holy"; Readable "아주 거룩한 것"
decisions.reason: "지극히 거룩한" is the term sheet's adjective for the Most Holy Place (지성소) and the most holy portions, so the link is heard in Korean.

records.literal_gloss: And went out [a] son of [an] Israelite woman — and he [was a] son of [an] Egyptian man — among the sons of Israel; and they fought in the camp, the son of the Israelite [woman] and [a] man, the Israelite.

en.L: And the son of an Israelite woman, and he [was] the son of an Egyptian man, went out among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and the son of the Israelite [woman] and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
en.B: A man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian went out among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. In the camp he got into a fight with an Israelite man.
en.R: There was a man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was from Egypt. He went out among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He and an Israelite man got into a fight in the camp.

es.L: Y salió el hijo de una mujer israelita —y él [era] hijo de un hombre egipcio— entre los hijos de Israel; y riñeron en el campamento el hijo de la [mujer] israelita y un hombre israelita.

es.R: Había un hombre cuya madre era israelita y cuyo padre era de Egipto. Él salió entre los israelitas. Él y un hombre israelita se pelearon en el campamento.

fr.B: Un homme dont la mère était israélite et le père égyptien sortit parmi les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Dans le camp, il se battit avec un Israélite.
fr.R: Il y avait un homme dont la mère était israélite et dont le père venait d’Égypte. Il est sorti parmi les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Lui et un Israélite se sont battus dans le camp.

vi.L: Con trai của một người đàn bà Y-sơ-ra-ên, và người ấy [là] con trai của một người đàn ông Ai Cập, đi ra giữa con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên; rồi con trai của người đàn bà Y-sơ-ra-ên ấy và một người đàn ông Y-sơ-ra-ên đánh nhau trong trại quân.

vi.R: Có một người đàn ông, mẹ là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, còn cha là người Ai Cập. Người ấy đi ra giữa dân Y-sơ-ra-ên. Người ấy và một người đàn ông Y-sơ-ra-ên đánh nhau trong khu trại.

ko.L: 그리고 한 이스라엘 여자의 아들이 나갔는데, 그는 이집트 남자의 아들이었다. [그가] 이스라엘 자손 가운데로 [나갔고], 그 이스라엘 여자의 아들과 한 이스라엘 남자가 진 안에서 싸웠다.
ko.B: 어머니는 이스라엘 사람이고 아버지는 이집트 사람인 한 남자가 이스라엘 백성 가운데로 나갔다. 그는 진 안에서 한 이스라엘 남자와 싸움이 붙었다.
ko.R: 어떤 남자가 있었는데, 그의 어머니는 이스라엘 사람이고 아버지는 이집트 사람이었다. 그가 이스라엘 사람들 가운데로 나갔다. 그리고 그와 한 이스라엘 남자가 진 안에서 싸움을 벌였다.

decisions.choice: the son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian man: a man of mixed descent
decisions.reason: A "mixed crowd" of non-Israelites went up from Egypt with Israel (Exodus 12:38; Numbers 11:4). This man's mother was an Israelite, but his father was an Egyptian, so he would be counted as belonging to his father's people rather than to an Israelite tribe. The narrator stresses this, and the ruling that follows says twice that the same law holds for the outsider and the native-born (verses 16 and 22).

decisions.choice: fought: the two men struggled with each other
decisions.reason: The verb means to struggle or brawl, of two people fighting each other (Exodus 2:13; 21:22; Deuteronomy 25:11). The text does not say who began it or what the quarrel was about. The story is told for what was said during it (verse 11).

decisions.choice: went out: he went out among the Israelites, from where is not said
decisions.reason: The text does not say where he came from. It may mean that he went out of his family's tent, or that he went among the tribes where he did not belong. The point is that the fight happened among the people, "in the camp".

decisions.choice: a man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "the son of an Israelite woman, and he was the son of an Egyptian man". Balanced and Readable describe him by his mother and father in one clause, and Readable breaks the verse into three short sentences.

decisions.choice: "진" for the camp at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for Israel's camp in the wilderness.

en.B: The Israelite woman's son blasphemed the Name, uttering curses, and they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, Dibri's daughter, of the tribe of Dan.

fr.R: Pendant la bagarre, le fils de la femme israélite a insulté le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et a lancé des malédictions. Alors les gens l’ont amené à Moïse. Sa mère s’appelait Shelomith. Elle était la fille de Dibri, de la tribu de Dan.

sw.L: Na mwana wa mwanamke Mwisraeli akalikufuru Jina, akalaani; nao wakamleta kwa Musa. Na jina la mama yake [lilikuwa] Shelomithi, binti Dibri, wa kabila la Dani.
sw.B: Mwana wa mwanamke Mwisraeli alilikufuru Jina kwa kutoa laana, nao wakamleta kwa Musa. Mama yake aliitwa Shelomithi, binti wa Dibri, wa kabila la Dani.
sw.R: Wakati wa ugomvi huo, mwana wa mwanamke Mwisraeli alilitukana jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kutoa laana. Kwa hiyo watu wakamleta kwa Musa. Mama yake aliitwa Shelomithi. Alikuwa binti wa Dibri, wa kabila la Dani.

vi.L: Con trai của người đàn bà Y-sơ-ra-ên ấy phạm thượng đến Danh và nguyền rủa, và người ta đem người ấy đến cùng Môi-se. Tên mẹ người ấy [là] Sê-lô-mít, con gái của Điệp-ri, thuộc chi tộc Đan.
vi.B: Con trai người đàn bà Y-sơ-ra-ên ấy phạm thượng đến Danh và buông lời nguyền rủa, nên người ta dẫn người ấy đến với Môi-se. Mẹ người ấy tên là Sê-lô-mít, con gái Điệp-ri, thuộc chi tộc Đan.
vi.R: Trong lúc đánh nhau, con trai của người đàn bà Y-sơ-ra-ên ấy xúc phạm danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và nguyền rủa. Vì vậy người ta dẫn anh ta đến với Môi-se. Mẹ anh ta tên là Sê-lô-mít. Bà là con gái của Điệp-ri, thuộc chi tộc Đan.

ko.L: 그리고 그 이스라엘 여자의 아들이 그 이름을 모독하고 저주했다. 그래서 그들이 그를 모세에게 데려갔다. 그의 어머니의 이름은 슬로밋이었는데, 단 지파 디브리의 딸이었다.
ko.B: 그 이스라엘 여자의 아들이 저주를 퍼부으며 그 이름을 모독했다. 그래서 사람들이 그를 모세에게 데려갔다. 그의 어머니의 이름은 슬로밋인데, 단 지파 디브리의 딸이었다.
ko.R: 싸우는 중에 그 이스라엘 여자의 아들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 이름을 모욕하고 저주했다. 그래서 사람들이 그를 모세에게 데려갔다. 그의 어머니의 이름은 슬로밋이었다. 그 여자는 단 지파 디브리의 딸이었다.

decisions.choice: blasphemed: spoke against God's name with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb can come from a root meaning "to curse" (Numbers 23:8) or from one meaning "to pierce, mark out", which can also mean to name (Isaiah 62:2). Here it stands next to "and he cursed", and verse 16 sets the penalty for whoever does this to "the name of the LORD", so it means to speak against God's name with contempt. Later Jewish tradition read the verb here as "pronounce", and from this verse drew the custom of not saying the divine name aloud. Verse 16 points to an abusive use of the name, not to saying it at all.

decisions.choice: the Name: the name of the LORD, that is, Yahweh
decisions.reason: Verse 16 says in full what this verse leaves short: "the name of the LORD". God's name stands for God himself as he has made himself known (Exodus 3:14-15; 34:5-7), and to misuse it is forbidden in the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:7). Leviticus warns against profaning the name in 18:21; 19:12; 22:2, 32.

decisions.choice: cursed: treated God with contempt, called down evil on him
decisions.reason: The verb comes from a root meaning "be light": to curse is to treat as worthless, the opposite of honoring. "You shall not curse God" is a law of the covenant (Exodus 22:28), and verse 15 names God as the one cursed. The verb has no object here; verses 14 and 23 call the man "the one who cursed".

decisions.choice: Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan: the man's Israelite mother
decisions.reason: The man himself is not named, but his mother is, with her father and tribe. Naming her family shows that the case touched a real Israelite household and tribe. Neither she nor Dibri is mentioned anywhere else in Scripture.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD; During the fight
decisions.reason: Readable writes "the name of the LORD" for "the Name", as verse 16 says, and "insulted" for "blasphemed". It adds "During the fight" to link this verse with verse 10, and "the people" as the subject of "brought".

decisions.choice: uttering curses
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two verbs, "blasphemed the Name, uttering curses", because "cursed" has no object in the Hebrew and describes how he blasphemed. Literal keeps "and cursed".

decisions.choice: blasfemó contra el Nombre (L, B); insultó el nombre del SEÑOR (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "blasfemar contra" is the ordinary construction for speaking against God; "el Nombre" keeps the capital of "the Name". Readable uses the commoner "insultar", as the English does; the same forms are used in verse 16.

decisions.choice: blasphéma le Nom (L, B); a insulté le nom du SEIGNEUR (R)
decisions.reason: "Blasphémer" is the French word for speaking against God with contempt (see m1), and "le Nom" keeps the capital of the English "the Name". Readable follows the English with the commoner "insulter"; the same forms are used in verse 16.

decisions.choice: alilikufuru Jina (L, B); alilitukana jina la BWANA (R)
decisions.reason: "Kukufuru" is speaking against God (see m1), with the object prefix agreeing with "Jina"; Readable uses the commoner "kutukana" (insult), as the English does. "Kulaani" is kept for "curse". The same forms are used in verse 16.

decisions.choice: "그 이름을 모독하다" for blaspheming the Name (Readable "모욕하다")
decisions.reason: "모독하다" is the current word for speaking against what is holy; the older "훼방하다" now means to obstruct. Readable uses the plainer "모욕하다", as the English Readable says "insulted".

decisions.choice: "슬로밋", "디브리" for the names Shelomith and Dibri
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean forms of these names.

decisions.choice: "Danh", capitalised (the Name)
decisions.reason: The Name stands for the LORD's own name, so it is capitalised as a title; Readable says "danh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Sê-lô-mít, con gái của Điệp-ri"
decisions.reason: Names not in the term sheet, in their usual Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: to make it clear by the mouth of the LORD: to receive the LORD's own ruling
decisions.reason: No law yet given covered this case, so they waited for a decision from God himself. "By the mouth of" means by his spoken word or command. The same verb for making a decision clear is used of the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath, also kept in custody until the LORD gave a ruling (Numbers 15:34); compare Numbers 9:8 and 27:5, where Moses brings a case before the LORD.

decisions.choice: custody: under guard
decisions.reason: The word means a place or act of guarding. It does not suggest a prison; the man was held so that he could not leave until the decision came.

decisions.choice: waiting for a clear ruling from the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what they were waiting for: the LORD's decision. Literal keeps "to make it clear to them by the mouth of the LORD".

decisions.choice: "주의 입으로 ... 밝혀지기를 [기다렸다]" keeps "by the mouth of the LORD" at Literal
decisions.reason: Korean needs a main verb for the purpose clause, so "기다렸다" is supplied in brackets; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: all who heard lean their hands on his head: the witnesses mark him as the one guilty of what they heard
decisions.reason: Those who heard the curse are the witnesses. The same gesture is used with offerings (1:4) and with the goat on the Day of Atonement (16:21). The text does not explain it here; it at least shows that the witnesses identify him as guilty and that the guilt of the words they heard rests on him, not on them or on the community.

decisions.choice: outside the camp: the sentence is carried out away from where God dwells among his people
decisions.reason: The camp was holy because the LORD's tent stood in it (Numbers 5:2-3). Executions took place outside it, as with the Sabbath-breaker (Numbers 15:35-36), and later outside the town (Deuteronomy 17:5).

decisions.choice: all the congregation shall stone him: the whole community carries out the sentence
decisions.reason: Stoning was carried out by the people together, not by one executioner, so that the whole community took responsibility for removing the evil from among them (20:2; Numbers 15:35; Deuteronomy 17:7).

decisions.choice: throw stones at him until he dies
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stone" as throwing stones until he dies, since the stoning is the death sentence (verse 16).

decisions.choice: lapider (L, B); jeter des pierres jusqu'à ce qu'il meure (R)
decisions.reason: "Lapider" is the precise French word for putting to death by stoning, as in Exodus 21 and Numbers 15; Readable spells it out, as the English does, since not every reader knows "lapider".

decisions.choice: "온 회중" for all the congregation; "돌로 치다" for stoning (Readable "돌을 던져 죽이다")
decisions.reason: "회중" is the term sheet's word for the congregation; Readable says "모든 사람" and spells out the stoning, as the English Readable does.

fr.R: Dis aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} : “Si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} maudit Dieu, cette personne est coupable et sera punie pour ce péché.
